key_inputs: Registered voters 7,331,981 on the CEC roll (gov.il voter guide, updated 12 Oct 2026, figure as of the final station map; repeated by Israel National News on 26 Oct). Turnout is ballots cast divided by that roll. 2022 was 70.63% of 6,788,804.

Final polls of 21-23 Oct, coalition defined as Likud+Shas+UTJ+RZP-Zehut+Otzma: Midgam/Channel 12 50, Madad/Channel 13 50, Kantar/Kan 50, Lazar/Maariv 48, Kantar/Israel Hayom 50, Tatika/Zman Yisrael 51. Direct Polls/i24 55 if Amcha is excluded and 59 if it is included. Filber/Channel 14 62.

Judgement: believe the five-firm cluster, not Filber. His +9 to +11 seat house effect is stable across the campaign, on a channel-owned digital panel with samples often near 500, and is much larger than his 2022 edge. Apply only the 2022-style correction those firms actually showed: the bloc they polled at 60 won 64, and Shas polled at 8 won 11. A 2015-sized Likud jump (+8) is the upper tail, not the centre, because Otzma and RZP are already measured in agreement across firms.

Threshold calls: Reservists 2.9% and Amcha 2.3% fail. They passed in some Kantar/Lazar/Tatika polls and in Direct Polls (Amcha only) but missed Channel 12 (2.4% and 2.5%) and Channel 13 (3.0% and 3.1%). Sapir Analytics on 26 Oct put their pass chances near 12% and 10%. Blue and White is off the ballot after every candidate resigned (21 Oct). Ahi quit on 23 Oct and endorsed Likud. Noam, Black Colour and the remaining fringe are inside other.

Surplus pairs used in the seat split: Likud+RZP-Zehut, Shas+UTJ, Yashar+Democrats, Together+Yisrael Beiteinu, Joint List+Ra'am. Otzma has no partner. Shares above were run through that Bader-Ofer allocation.

notes: The forecast follows Midgam, Kantar, Lazar, Madad and Tatika, who clustered the five coalition lists near 50 seats, and treats Channel 14's 62 as a house effect rather than a hidden electorate. A 2022-sized correction, not a 2015-sized one, lifts Shas to 9 and Likud to 22, leaving Yashar the largest list at 23 and the coalition at 52. Amcha and the Reservists stay under 3.25%, so their votes are wasted rather than turned into four-seat factions. Arab parties stay at 14 because the reunited Joint List is already in the polls and the 'record turnout' talk looks like the Zehut overrate of April 2019. Social signals moved about one seat, toward Likud, through Netanyahu's 26 October call not to waste ballots on Winter, and did not add seats for Arab or Reservist hype.
